_about: GSTR-3B canonical layer - how each line of the 3B form is recognised (spec: docs/GSTR3B_CANONICAL_SPEC.md). A line is found by its LABEL text, never by row or column position. Each rule is tested on the row's text ('text' = every non-empty cell of the row joined with a space). Rule keys (all that are present must hold): 'all' = every substring appears (case-sensitive); 'any' = at least one appears; 'none' = none appears; 'lower_all' = every substring appears ignoring case; 'startswith' = the stripped row text starts with it. A rule with 'section' only looks between the row whose text starts with section.start and the row whose text starts with section.end, and needs 'row_startswith' (tested in the order given by 'row_startswith', first hit wins per row) plus at least one number on the row. 'required': true means the month cannot be processed without the line (ERROR); otherwise a missing line is a WARNING and the engine treats it as absent. To support a reworded form line, add its wording to the right rule. 'absent_ok': true = the line legitimately does not exist in newer forms, so its absence is INFO, not a warning.
